passage:
At preschool, Lalit sir held a puppet behind his back. "Who's coming?" he whispered in a deep voice.
The children went still. Then a squeaky "Meeeep!" burst out and the puppet popped over his shoulder, a spoon on its head.
Santosh screamed with laughter and fell back on the mat, kicking his feet. "Again! Again!"
Lalit sir did it again, with a "Honk!" this time. Santosh laughed so hard he got hiccups. When Lalit sir said the puppet's name wrong on purpose, Santosh shouted, "No, it's Bunty!"
Then he crawled over and leaned against Lalit sir's arm.

qa.q: What was the puppet wearing on its head?
qa.a: The puppet had a spoon on its head.

qa.q: What was Santosh feeling when the puppet squeaked and popped over Lalit sir's shoulder?
qa.a: Santosh was delighted and amused, screaming with laughter, kicking his feet and calling for it again.

qa.q: How could a grown-up keep this kind of play going safely?
qa.a: A grown-up could repeat the surprise in a gentle way, like a silly voice or a wrong word, and stay close so the child feels safe while laughing.

qa.q: What might Lalit sir be feeling when Santosh leans against his arm?
qa.a: Lalit sir probably feels warm and pleased. The child's trust after all the laughing shows the play has brought them close.

grounding: A child giggles at surprises and silly sounds, and laughing together bonds him to a caregiver.

passage:
I'm Nilesh. From my balcony I watch five-year-old Damini play in the garden with her Dada. Yesterday he put his hat on upside down. Damini stopped, stared, and burst out laughing.
"That's not how you wear it!" He looked puzzled, put it on backwards. She laughed until she sat on the grass.
Then he called a dog a "cow" in a serious voice. "Dada! It's a dog!" Each time she looked at his face first, checking he was joking.
I can only guess what it's like for her, but she kept running back to him, and he kept smiling.

qa.q: How old is Damini?
qa.a: Damini is five years old.

qa.q: What was Damini feeling when her Dada put his hat on upside down?
qa.a: Damini was amused and delighted, stopping to stare and then laughing until she sat on the grass.

qa.q: What does Damini's habit of checking Dada's face before laughing suggest about what she is thinking?
qa.a: It suggests Damini wants to be sure he is joking and that the silliness is safe. Her trust in him lets her laugh.

qa.q: What might Dada be feeling as Damini runs back after each silly thing?
qa.a: Dada is probably happy and affectionate, since he keeps smiling and keeps playing. Her laughter seems to please him as much as it pleases her.

grounding: A child laughs at silly behaviour from a safe adult, and an observer sees how laughing together builds trust.

passage:
"Yusuf, where's your nose?" asked Lokesh bhaiya, the neighbour who babysat on Tuesdays.
Yusuf, four, pointed at his nose.
"No! That's your ELBOW!"
Yusuf shrieked with laughter. "No, it's my NOSE!"
"Then what's this?" Lokesh bhaiya touched Yusuf's knee. "Is this your ear?"
"NO!" Yusuf was rolling on the rug now. "It's my knee, silly!"
"Oh. Then I must be a potato."
"You're not a potato!" Yusuf giggled so hard he got hiccups. Then he climbed onto Lokesh bhaiya's lap. "Again. Do the elbow one again."
"Where's your nose, Yusuf?"
Yusuf pointed, already giggling. "Elbow!"

qa.q: What did Lokesh bhaiya say Yusuf's nose was?
qa.a: He said it was Yusuf's ELBOW.

qa.q: How can you tell Yusuf felt safe and happy with Lokesh bhaiya?
qa.a: He rolled on the rug giggling, climbed into Lokesh bhaiya's lap and asked for the joke again.

qa.q: What could Lokesh bhaiya try next to keep the fun going?
qa.a: He could let Yusuf be the one who names things wrong, so Yusuf gets to make the silly surprises too.

qa.q: What is it like for Lokesh bhaiya when Yusuf climbs into his lap?
qa.a: He probably feels warm and pleased, since the silly game has made Yusuf trust him more.

grounding: Shows a young child giggling at wrong words in a safe game, and laughing together bonding him to a caregiver.

passage:
Nursery note, Monday.
At story time I held up the picture of a cat and said, "Look, a big dog!" Pankaj (4) stared at me, then burst out laughing. "That's a CAT!" I said, "Oh no, then it must say moo." He laughed so hard he fell sideways onto Tushar, who giggled too, though I'm not sure he knew why.
All session Pankaj kept checking my face: "Say the wrong one again!" He is usually quiet and clingy at drop-off, so this was lovely.
I told his mother at pickup. Tomorrow I'll let him hold the pictures and name them wrong for me.

qa.q: What animal was in the picture at story time?
qa.a: A cat.

qa.q: What does Pankaj checking the teacher's face suggest about him?
qa.a: It suggests he felt safe and delighted with the teacher, wanting more of the surprise game from someone he trusts.

qa.q: What did the note-writer plan next, and why is it a good idea?
qa.a: Letting Pankaj hold the pictures and name them wrong lets him lead the joke, building his confidence and their bond.

qa.q: What was it like for Tushar during the game?
qa.a: Tushar laughed along, probably enjoying the shared fun even if he didn't fully get the joke.

grounding: Shows a young child giggling at a wrong word in a safe setting, and shared laughter helping him bond with his teacher.

passage: In the courtyard of Dadi's house in Barmer, the goat said "Baa!" and Wasim, five, looked up from his marbles. Dadi said "Baa!" right back, in a deep, silly voice. Wasim froze, then giggled. The goat said "Baa!" again. Dadi said "BAA!" even louder, pulling a big-eyed face. Wasim fell off the charpai laughing. Cousin Sumit peeked over the wall to see what was funny. Then Dadi hid behind the haystack. "Where did Dadi go?" Sumit whispered. Wasim crept close, and Dadi popped out: "Baa!" Wasim screamed with joy and wrapped his arms around her neck. "Do it again, Dadi!"

qa.q: Where did Dadi hide?
qa.a: Behind the haystack.

qa.q: How can you tell Wasim felt close to Dadi after the game?
qa.a: He screamed with joy and wrapped his arms around her neck, asking her to do it again.

qa.q: How could Sumit join in the fun?
qa.a: Sumit could take a turn hiding and popping out with a silly 'Baa!' so Wasim gets another safe surprise.

qa.q: What might Dadi enjoy about playing with Wasim like this?
qa.a: She probably loves hearing him laugh and feeling him hug her, which brings them closer.

grounding: Shows a young child laughing at a silly surprise from a grandmother, and shared laughter strengthening their bond.

passage: In the small kitchen in Bergen, Pappa held up a mitten. "Here's your hat, Ingrid." Ingrid squealed. "That's not a hat! That's a MITTEN!" Anders put it on his head anyway, very seriously. Ingrid laughed so hard she slid off her chair. "Now your boots," he said, and handed her a banana. She shrieked and hid behind the fridge door, then popped out with "Boo!" Her pappa jumped as if he was terribly scared. They were both still laughing when Mamma came in, and neither of them could explain why.

qa.q: What did Anders hand Ingrid when he said "Now your boots"?
qa.a: He handed her a banana.

qa.q: Why did Ingrid laugh so hard she slid off her chair?
qa.a: She felt delighted by the silly mix-up 😄 Her pappa called a mitten a hat and then wore it very seriously.

qa.q: What could Anders try on a grumpy morning to bring back the same fun?
qa.a: He could use one small silly mix-up, like calling a spoon a sock, and let Ingrid correct him.

qa.q: How might Mamma see the scene when she walks in?
qa.a: Mamma may feel puzzled but warm, seeing the two of them close and laughing even without knowing the joke.

grounding: Shows a young child giggling at wrong words and a sudden surprise and sharing the laughter with a parent.
